summary:
Astronaut Health Check-in is a web app that helps astronauts spot changes in their own health and decide what to do next, when help is far away.

We built a daily check-in for nine indicators: blood pressure, heart rate, glucose, temperature, sleep, exercise, mood and stress. Each reading becomes OK, Watch or Act, with three short sentences: what it means, what to do, and when to tell the crew doctor. A dashboard, body map and trend charts show how health is changes over time, and a Calm Break page offers a quiet moment.

It addresses the challenge by gathering health indicators and letting astronauts evaluate and act on their own status. This matters because on long missions with radiation, isolation and altered gravity, astronauts carry much of the responsibility for noticing problems early. We used clear rules instead of machine learning, so every alert can be explained, and we included real NASA Inspiration4 blood-test data as a reference.
details:
Astronaut Health Check-in is a web app that helps astronauts spot changes in their own health and decide what to do next, when help is far away.

WHAT IT DOES: An astronaut logs a daily check-in with nine readings: blood pressure (top and bottom), resting heart rate, fasting glucose, body temperature, sleep, exercise, mood and stress. Each reading is shown as OK, Watch or Act, with three short sentences: what it means, what to do, and when to tell the crew doctor. Advice differs for "too low" and "too high". The app also has a dashboard with an overall score, a Body Map, Trends charts, Mission Tasks, a Learn page, and a Calm Break page with a star game and guided breathing (no timer, no score).

HOW IT WORKS: Clear rules, not machine learning, so every alert can be explained.

DATA: The daily log is simulated for one pretend astronaut. We also included real Inspiration4 blood tests from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSD-569, OSD-575). NASA research on spaceflight health risks shaped our indicators and advice.

IMPACT: Astronauts on long missions must notice changes in themselves. The app gives a quick view of their health, clear next steps, and trends that show slow changes early.

TOOLS: Python, Streamlit, pandas, Plotly, GitHub, Streamlit Community Cloud.

LIMITS: Common adult ranges, not spaceflight limits. Decision support, not a diagnosis.
dataRefs: Inspiration4 data in NASA OSDR (OSD-569, OSD-575)
